title: How bonding and structure are related to the properties of substances
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.2.2-c12, 4.2.2-c22, 4.2.2-c19, 4.2.2-c18. Clues: 4.2.2-c12 written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c22 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c19 written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c18 written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: 4.2.2-q13, 4.2.2-q26, 4.2.2-q30, 4.2.2-q32, 4.2.2-q14, 4.2.2-q27, 4.2.2-q31, 4.2.2-q15.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Aqueous solution (aq)
items.clue: Made by dissolving a substance in water.

items.label: Polymer
items.clue: A substance whose molecules are very large.

items.label: Covalent bond
items.clue: A shared pair of electrons holding two atoms together.

items.label: Intermolecular force
items.clue: The weak attraction between one molecule and its neighbour.

questions.stem: What does the state symbol (aq) tell you about a substance in an equation?

options.text: It is a liquid, whether or not it is water
It is the water used as the solvent here
It is a gas bubbled through the mixture
It is dissolved in water to give a solution

questions.explanation: (aq) shows an aqueous solution, that is a substance dissolved in water.

questions.stem: Why is poly(ethene) a solid at room temperature?

options.text: Covalent bonds join each polymer chain to the next one
It is a giant covalent structure just like diamond
Its molecules are far too heavy to move at all
Its very large molecules attract each other strongly

questions.explanation: Because polymer molecules are very large, the intermolecular forces between them are relatively strong.

questions.stem: Why do most metals have high melting points and boiling points?

options.text: The metallic bonding in the giant structure is strong
The atoms in a metal are heavy and packed very tightly
Metals are hard, and hard materials melt slowly
Delocalised electrons stop the atoms escaping

questions.explanation: Metals have giant structures of atoms with strong metallic bonding, so most have high melting and boiling points.

questions.stem: Why are metals good conductors of electricity and of thermal energy?

options.text: The metal ions are free to move around the metal
The atoms are packed so tightly that energy passes
Delocalised electrons carry charge and energy
Protons in the metal carry the electric charge along

questions.explanation: The delocalised electrons carry electrical charge through the metal and also transfer thermal energy.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon is added to dilute hydrochloric acid. Which equation has the correct state symbols?

options.text: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl2(aq) + H2(g)
Mg(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl2(aq) + H2(g)
Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl2(s) + H2(g)
Mg(s) + 2HCl(l) → MgCl2(s) + H2(g)

questions.explanation: The metal is solid, the acid and the salt are dissolved in water, and hydrogen is given off as a gas.

questions.stem: A diagram shows a long chain of carbon atoms joined by covalent bonds, with the chain continuing at both ends. What does it show?

options.text: A polymer built from large molecules
A giant covalent structure such as silica
A metal, since the atoms lie in a line
A small molecule such as ethene gas

questions.explanation: Continuation marks and a repeating covalently bonded chain identify a polymer molecule.

questions.stem: Why is an alloy usually harder than the pure metal it is made from?

options.text: The two metals react to make a new compound entirely
Atoms of different sizes stop the layers sliding
The alloy contains far more delocalised electrons
The added atoms are heavier and much harder

questions.explanation: In a pure metal the atoms are arranged in layers that can slide; different sized atoms disrupt those layers.

questions.stem: Calcium carbonate chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid. Which equation has the correct state symbols?

options.text: CaCO3(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + H2O(aq) + CO2(g)
CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g)
CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + H2O(aq) + CO2(g)
CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(l) → CaCl2(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g)

questions.explanation: The chips are solid, the acid and the salt are aqueous, the water is a pure liquid and carbon dioxide is a gas.
